newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian OTC market firms in busy week to June 27.
newsitem.headline: Croatian OTC market firms in busy week to June 27.

text.p: The Croatian over-the-counter market firmed in the week to June 27 amid bouyant activity, the Varazdin market reported on Monday.
The leading seven-stock VIN index rose 2.8 percent to 10,002 points as nine active issues rose, eight fell, six were flat and two traded for the first time.
Volume almost doubled to 99,246 shares and the total weekly turnover rose threefold to 16.3 million kuna.
Direct trade reported to the market by brokers accounted for 78,294 shares, mostly in various units of electrical group Koncar which is due for floatiation in about a year's time.
A 64,970-share package in department store Vama, which is being privatised, was sold for 3.6 million kuna. Only 16,594 shares were fully paid for to the state privatisation agency.
The most active Croatia Banka, firming 20 percent on a weekly basis to 180 kuna, sold 10,019 shares and accounted for 34 percent of the total trade.
Shipper Atlantska Plovidba was the biggest gainer, rising 61.82 percent to 178 kuna with 474 shares traded.
The biggest decliner was Dalmatinska Banka, falling 23.08 percent to 300 kuna on volume of 98 units.
Food group Podravka had a nine percent share in OTC trade with 1,791 shares sold, closing 5.36 percent lower at 265 kuna.
It did not fare well on the central bourse either, where it ended the week at 268 kuna compared to 275 a week earlier. But traders said the stock was moving in cycles and was bound to recover soon.
